policy_context.execution_authorization_reference: Current explicit owner instruction 2026-10-22 authorizes bounded exploratory M4 measurements and remeasurement after material instrumentation changes, using fresh operation IDs and full containment; no retry after a gate failure and no hard-gate bypass.
policy_context.resource_basis: One distinct, bounded paired experiment testing whether the opt-in ordered Upsert group-commit queue adds value when both arms use the existing WAL-preserving snapshot-rebase compaction. The direct and group-commit arms use identical 1,024-document seeds, four writers × eight individual Upsert calls, two search readers, one concurrent snapshot-rebase compaction, explicit flush, reopen verification and WAL fsync; resource and containment caps are unchanged. The paired direct arm distinguishes the queue effect within this operation; compare it descriptively with the separately consumed default-compaction profile only, not as a controlled four-way comparison. Capture per-call writer latency, group wait/size, state-lock and compaction stages, reader samples, fsync counts, and durability/reopen checks. One fresh operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried. No qualification, stable-tail claim, architecture win, or production authorization.
policy_context.risk_acceptance_reference: The standard contention profile is four-arm; writer_group_commit is a separate two-arm per-call Upsert experiment. All are descriptive only: shared-host pressure, one round per arm and test-scale workloads prohibit causal, qualification or architecture-win claims. ApplyBatch and Upsert call latencies have different units and must not be compared as equivalent tail samples.
